issue.title: Give ci_watch a watched-workflow notification list so heavy-lane failures page while their SHA is unsettled
issue.description: After epic sase-um moved sase's exhaustive suite onto the scheduled Full CI lane, a red Full CI run never reaches ci_watch's notification path: the ~1h43m run keeps its master tip unsettled in actstat, and actstat only emits a commit once every run attached to that SHA completes. Named as required follow-up by plan 202608/release_gate_liveness.md phase heavy. Proposed by the sase-um land agent.

task_type_fields.proposal:
Give `ci_watch` (in `bbugyi200/bugyi-chops`) a `watched_workflows` notification list: a
config var naming workflows whose failures must page through the chop's SASE
notification path regardless of whether the SHA they attach to has settled in actstat.

Today `classify_repo` / `decide_repo` drive notifications from actstat's settled-commit
record, and `select_settled_commits` (sase-core `src/github.rs`) only emits a commit
once *every* workflow run attached to that SHA has completed. Epic sase-um's `Full CI`
attaches a ~1h43m run to whatever master tip is current when its two-hour schedule
fires, so that tip stays unsettled for the whole run and a heavy-lane failure never
reaches the notification path.

Shape it like the `gating_workflows` allowlist sase-um.2 already added: evaluate it from
`GitHubReader`'s own bounded queries rather than from the actstat sweep, keep it empty
by default so every other repo the chop watches is unaffected, and reuse the existing
per-incident dedupe so one red `Full CI` run does not page every five-minute tick.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope:
Plan `202608/release_gate_liveness.md`, phase `heavy`, records this as an accepted cost
of moving the exhaustive lane off the push path and directs explicitly: "Enable GitHub's
native workflow-failure notifications for the repository, and file a task bead (via
`/sase_new_task`) to extend `ci_watch` with a watched-workflow notification list." It
was deliberately kept out of that epic because the epic's release gate does not read the
notification path at all -- it reads `gating_workflows` and the heavy-lane freshness
condition -- so nothing in sase-um's acceptance criteria depends on this, and it lands in
a different repository on its own release cadence.
